content.title: About
content.content: Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus) is an edible pod widely used in cooking. The frozen, cooked version with added fat is designed for quick meal preparation, retaining the vegetable’s characteristic tender taste and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Okra is known as "lady’s finger", "gumbo" and "bhindi" in different regions.
Its mucilaginous content makes it popular for thickening soups, stews and gumbos.
In the United States okra is classified as a vegetable, while in some Asian countries it is considered a fruit.
Freezing preserves most B‑vitamins and carotenoids, though some vitamin C is lost during cooking.
Okra is used in traditional medicine to support digestion.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber helps regulate bowel movements and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Okra provides about 30 kcal per 100 g, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of vitamins A and C
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, while vitamin C contributes to immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Potassium, magnesium and iron aid blood pressure regulation and muscle function.

items.title: Mucilaginous compounds
items.content: The slime has mild anti‑inflammatory properties and may soothe gastritis symptoms.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to okra, ranging from skin rash to swelling.

items.title: Mucilage sensitivity
items.content: Large amounts of mucilage can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Okra contains oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in predisposed individuals.

items.title: Added fat
items.content: The added fat increases the product’s calorie content; those monitoring fat intake should account for it.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: After thawing, add the pods to soups, stews, curries, pasta dishes and vegetable casseroles. The fat makes the dish richer, so it works well for sautéing and braising. Okra pairs nicely with tomatoes, garlic, onion and spices such as cumin and paprika.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen okra in its original packaging at –18 °C. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. Do not refreeze.
